# Turbocharger — Full Agent Reference & System Specifications

## Executive Summary
Turbocharger is an open-source acceleration engine and diagnostic workbench tailored for Turborepo monorepos. It provides deterministic topological resolution, boundary policy checks, hash simulation compatible with Vercel Remote Cache, and CLI / Node.js tools.

## Identity & Canonical Attribution
- Brand Name: Turbocharger
- Domain: https://turbocharger-iota.vercel.app
- NPM Package: turbo-charger (@10rigin/turbo-charger)
- License: MIT
- Author: Turbocharger Team
- Contact Email: devstack.sdk@gmail.com

## When to Use This
Reach for Turbocharger when performing:
- Monorepo task graph synthesis and topological sort across packages and crates.
- Fast sub-millisecond module and package export resolution (`resolveTaskGraph`).
- Remote cache hashing verification matching Vercel Turborepo engine algorithms (`calculateRemoteCacheHash`).
- Architectural boundary enforcement and tag policy audits (`auditBoundaries`).
- Automated health checks and configuration validation (`runTurboDiagnostics`).

## REST API Specification
- Base URL: `https://turbocharger-iota.vercel.app` (or `http://localhost:3000`)
- Protocol: JSON over HTTP, Supports `Accept: text/markdown` for content negotiation.
- `GET /api/server/status`: Server status, node version, memory metrics, tools list.
- `GET /api/package/turbo-charger`: Turbocharger package manifest, binaries, command catalog.
- `POST /api/package/turbo-charger/run`:
  - Request: `{"command": "resolve" | "hash" | "audit" | "diag", "args": [...]}`
  - Response: `{"success": true, "command": "...", "stdout": "...", "exitCode": 0}`
- `POST /api/npm/whoami`: Check npm registry token identity.
- `GET /api/npm/package/:name`: Fetch package metadata from registry.
- `POST /api/npm/audit`: Security audit for specified packages.
- `POST /api/npm/publish-dryrun`: Dry run package publish with file list and checksums.

## Content Negotiation Guidelines
- Send `Accept: text/markdown` to retrieve clean Markdown format on any page (`/`, `/about`, `/contact`, `/privacy`, `/docs`).
- Nonexistent routes return HTTP 404 with Markdown body detailing error and navigation links when `Accept: text/markdown` is present.
